memories.content: Specify a single representative measure that serves as the criterion for retaining, modifying, or discarding compared design alternatives.
HCI review panels verify whether clear criteria for judging design alternatives are established using the declared primary measure.
Collect process measures to diagnose interaction steps where problems occurred, alongside the primary outcome measure.
Interpret evaluation results as differences between compared design alternatives rather than as success or failure of a single prototype.
Check boundary cases to verify whether the derived design principles retain explanatory power for adjacent situations not included in the comparison.
Controlled evaluation environments do not reproduce time pressure, peer intervention, or voluntary termination conditions found in daily use.
Do not change names referring to the same user roles, system functions, or operational stages midway.
Use abbreviations only for long recurring terms in a two-page proposal.
Present the full term and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Refer to participants based on the roles they perform in the study rather than their status.
Reviewers from different subfields find it difficult to infer an abbreviation from context alone when it is not defined at first use.
When introducing an operational role for the first time, define both the decisions it can make and the actions it performs.
Individuals holding identical job titles may possess different system modification privileges and data access rights depending on their deployment site.
The user tends to group distinct field roles under the single label “user.”

analysis.overview: The frames address separate concerns: the reference frame governs comparative HCI evaluation, while the compared frame governs precise terminology for abbreviations and operational roles. Neither supplies a scope-qualified counterpart to the other, and no contradiction is present.

relations.reason: These statements split one one-sided policy into establishment of the decision criterion and verification that it is properly established.
relations.summary: A declared primary measure should govern judgments among design alternatives, with review panels checking that this criterion is clear.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame supplies this independently useful diagnostic-measure requirement.
relations.summary: Process measures should accompany the primary outcome measure to locate problematic interaction steps.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame specifies this comparative interpretation policy.
relations.summary: Evaluation results should be interpreted as differences among alternatives rather than as a verdict on one prototype.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame provides this generalization check.
relations.summary: Derived design principles should be tested against adjacent, previously unexamined situations for continued explanatory power.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame identifies this ecological-validity limitation.
relations.summary: Controlled evaluations omit important daily-use conditions such as time pressure, peer intervention, and voluntary termination.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame states this terminology-consistency rule.
relations.summary: Names for recurring roles, functions, and stages should remain consistent throughout a document.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame supplies this independent restriction on when abbreviations are warranted.
relations.summary: In a short proposal, abbreviations should be reserved for long terms that recur.

relations.reason: The statements express one one-sided first-use definition requirement and its supporting accessibility rationale.
relations.summary: An abbreviation should be paired with its full term at first use because readers across subfields may not infer it reliably.

relations.reason: Each statement contributes to one underlying role-description policy by specifying operational grounding or explaining why broad labels fail to capture meaningful capability differences.
relations.summary: Participants should be represented by explicitly defined operational roles because status, job titles, and generic labels can obscure differences in duties and authority.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers naming consistency, restrained and defined abbreviations, and role descriptions grounded in actual responsibilities and permissions rather than broad labels or status.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame covers primary and diagnostic measures, comparative interpretation, boundary-case testing, and limits of controlled environments.
